ai.description: This frog reaches 3–4 cm. It is brown with a dark interorbital bar and pale throat. Key features include a rounded snout and smooth skin with sparse, small tubercles on the dorsum.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Limnonectes shompenorum* is best distinguished by its uniquely small body size and the presence of distinct, prominent glandular folds on its skin compared to larger congeners.
ai.habitat: The Shompen Frog inhabits primary tropical evergreen rainforests on Great Nicobar Island, typically found near small, slow-moving streams at low to moderate elevations.
ai.behavior: The Shompen frog is primarily nocturnal, foraging for small invertebrates along the forest floor and near stream banks under the cover of darkness.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Limnonectes shompenorum* is an oviparous frog that likely breeds during the monsoon season, laying small clutches of large, unpigmented eggs in terrestrial nests.
ai.distributionRemarks: The Shompen frog is endemic to Great Nicobar Island in the Andaman and Nicobar archipelago, occurring at low to moderate elevations within tropical rainforests.
ai.callDescription: The Shompen Frog emits a high-pitched, rhythmic series of short, metallic chirps while perched near small, rocky forest streams in the Nicobar Islands.
